findings.property: The supported isolated Python action must not execute unpinned site startup code before its directly pinned script.
findings.evidence: The contract requires -I (or a grouped equivalent) so caller/site startup code cannot be another executable source. Python -I implies -E, -P and -s, but does not imply -S. The system site module still runs at interpreter initialization; its global .pth executable lines and sitecustomize can execute code before the pinned script. Those files are not required to be in the candidate pins. Thus the plan's startup-source claim is stronger than the specified argv form. This is confirmed by Python's command-line and site documentation: -I disables the user site, while -S disables importing site; site documents that .pth import lines execute at startup and sitecustomize may perform arbitrary customization.
findings.falsifier: Require -S together with -I in the closed supported Python form, add -S to the explicit option allowlist, and test that the accepted action has site disabled; or narrow the contract to caller-controlled environment/user-site startup and explicitly put system site initialization under the trusted runtime boundary. Keep the direct script pin and all four source-v2 behavioral REDs.

assessment.source_v2_findings: The resolved-interpreter directory case, Python stdin source, Bash stdin source, and inherited stdin for opaque commands are each addressed with concrete refusals or DEVNULL and focused behavioral REDs before source edits.
assessment.workflow_boundary: Correctly preserves the missing historical evidence, does not treat replay as historical RED, and grants neither governance waiver nor activation/T218 authorization.
assessment.feasibility: The test-only stage and root inspection boundary are concrete and feasible; suite fixture changes and actual marker-based REDs are specified.
